commit_message:
Offload `lookupCommand` into IO threads when threaded IO is enabled (#13696)

From flame graph, we could see `lookupCommand` in main thread costs much
CPU, so we can let IO threads to perform `lookupCommand`.

To avoid race condition among multiple IO threads, made the following
changes:
- Pause all IO threads when register or unregister commands
- Force a full rehashing of the command table dict when resizing

findings.title: Data race on adjacent bit-fields of struct dict when lookupCommand is offloaded to IO threads
findings.message: PR #13696 changed processInputBuffer() so that, when an I/O thread is handling a client (c->running_tid != IOTHREAD_MAIN_THREAD_ID), it calls lookupCommand(c->argv, c->argc) directly from the I/O thread and caches the result in c->iolookedcmd, instead of deferring the whole lookup to the main thread. lookupCommand() ends up calling dictFind() on server.commands, which reads the dict's `useStoredKeyApi : 1` bit-field. That bit-field is packed into the same storage word as the `pauserehash : 15` bit-field in `struct dict` (src/dict.h). The main thread concurrently mutates `pauserehash` (e.g. via dictPauseRehashing/dictResumeRehashing invoked while iterating with dictNext()), which requires a non-atomic read-modify-write of the entire shared storage unit. Because C bit-fields sharing a machine word are not individually atomic, a main-thread RMW on `pauserehash` racing with an IO-thread read of `useStoredKeyApi` on the very same word constitutes a data race (confirmed by ThreadSanitizer/ASAN). Before this commit, lookupCommand()/dictFind() on server.commands was only ever executed on the main thread, so no concurrent access to this shared storage word existed; this commit is what introduces genuine multi-threaded access to the racy bit-fields.
findings.suggestion: Do not share a storage unit between a bit-field that is mutated concurrently from the main thread (pauserehash, via dictNext()/dictPauseRehashing) and a bit-field that is read from other threads (useStoredKeyApi), for dicts such as server.commands that can be looked up from I/O threads. Either give pauserehash a full-width, non-bitfield type (as ultimately done in the ac tual fix) so mutating it cannot perform an RMW on neighboring bits, or avoid calling lookupCommand()/dictFind() on server.commands from I/O threads altogether without additional synchronization.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two logically-independent bit-fields (pauserehash and useStoredKeyApi) inside struct dict share the same underlying storage unit, so a write to one requires a non-atomic read-modify-write that can race with a concurrent read/write of the other. This latent structural hazard became an actual exploitable/observable data race once PR #13696 introduced concurrent, unsynchronized access to the command dict (server.commands) from I/O threads via lookupCommand()->dictFind(), racing with the main thread's rehash-pause bookkeeping on the same dict.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Data race on adjacent bit-fields of struct dict when lookupCommand is offloaded to IO threads
